Subject: CorpBank evaluation next steps & dataset/score format

Hi Alex / Jane —

Great to meet you both today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our call:

- Goal: validate model fit for customer support triage & first-draft responses across 6 high-volume intent categories.
- Success criteria we heard: >= 85% macro-accuracy on intent classification, and mean preference score >= 4.0/5 for draft-response usefulness on a 200-sample blind eval.
- Redwood recommended starting models: llama-3-13b-q4f (efficient baseline), redwood-xl-8k (quality baseline), and an instruction-tuned distilled candidate for latency-sensitive flows.

Next steps we propose:
1) You share a 200–500 sample eval set (anonymized) in the attached schema (corpbank_eval_dataset_schema.csv).
2) Redwood runs 3 model variants with the attached prompt set (corpbank_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) and returns per-sample outputs + scoring breakdown.
3) We provide a one-pager with recommendations (model, quantization profile, batching targets) and a follow-up call for results and rollout plan.

Attachments: corpbank_eval_dataset_schema.csv, corpbank_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, redwood_eval_run_template.md

If that aligns, can you confirm by EOD Wed and share the dataset via the SharePoint link I sent? I can kick off the eval as soon as we have the file and a HubSpot deal number (we have CB-2026-142 on our side).

Thanks — talk soon.

— Marissa

Thanks Alex — this is perfect. A few notes and what we'll deliver in the run:

- Schema & PII: the attached CSV supports redaction flags (see col: pii_flag) and a free-text redaction_notes field. If you prefer, we can accept a redacted file or your original with pii_flag set; we have a scrub step in our eval pipeline.

- Scoring plan (we'll return):
  * Automated: intent accuracy (macro + micro), per-intent precision/recall, response overlap (ROUGE-L) vs. your gold responses, and latency percentiles for each model/quant profile.
  * Human: blind pairwise preference (n=200) with guidance doc attached — we'll randomize outputs across model variants and collect 1–5 usefulness & 1–5 fidelity scores.
  * Regression checks: we'll run an automated diff vs. your historical benchmarks (if you provide them) and flag any >5% drop in macro-accuracy or >0.5 drop in mean preference.

- Recommended model/quant profile for the run:
  1) llama-3-13b-q4f (fast baseline, expected median latency ~120ms/token on our Dedicated pool)
  2) redwood-xl-8k (quality baseline, expected mean preference improvement)
  3) redwood-instruct-distil (latency-optimized instruction-tuned candidate)

- Output format: JSONL with fields: sample_id, prompt, model, output, tokens, latency_ms, automated_scores (csv-string), human_pref_id (if evaluated). We include a run-level summary CSV and per-sample outputs.

- Timeline: once we get the data (you said Thurs AM), we'll schedule a run on Friday and share preliminary results by EOD Friday. Full human preference scoring and final report by Tue next week.

Attachments: redwood_eval_run_template.md (run checklist + JSONL output example)

If that aligns I’ll create the HubSpot activities and a dedicated eval project in our SharePoint and kick off the run when the file appears.

— Marissa
